title: Add tiered batching profile schema (fast/standard/cost-efficient) with validation + backcompat
author: Ethan Park
body: Summary: This PR introduces the config schema and validation needed to ship tiered batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient) while keeping backwards compatibility with existing per-route batching knobs. This is plumbing-only: it defines how tiers and optional per-tier profile overrides are expressed, validated, and surfaced to runtime config resolution. It does not change scheduler heuristics or default knob values; those land in follow-up PRs. Context: As part of workload-aware batching defaults, we need a stable, customer-facing tier concept that can be selected at the route/model policy level and overridden by enterprise/Dedicated configs. We also need to ensure customers with existing manual batching settings do not break, and that invalid or partially-specified configs fail fast with actionable error messages. What’s included: (1) New schema types: - Adds a new enum `BatchingSloTier` with values: `FAST`, `STANDARD`, `COST_EFFICIENT`. - Adds `batching.tier` to `RoutePolicy` (optional). If unset, the effective tier is `STANDARD` (subject to higher-precedence overrides in later work). - Adds `batching.profiles` (optional) for per-tier explicit knob overrides. This is intended primarily for internal benchmarking and Dedicated overrides; public docs will steer customers to tier selection rather than manual knob tuning. (2) Validation + guardrails: - Enforces that per-tier profiles, when present, include required knobs as an all-or-nothing set (prevents partial overrides that can create surprising behavior). - Validates numeric ranges for knob fields (e.g., wait budgets >= 0, token limits > 0) and cross-field constraints (e.g., `max_batch_tokens` >= `max_prefill_tokens_per_request` when both present). - Rejects unknown tier strings with explicit error output listing allowed values. (3) Backwards-compatible defaults / migration path: - Preserves the legacy batching config surface (`max_batch_tokens`, `max_wait_ms`, etc.) for existing customers and internal configs. - Adds a compatibility layer: if legacy knobs are present and `batching.tier` is not set, config resolution treats it as `tier=STANDARD` with an implicit `profiles[STANDARD]` override populated from legacy values (so existing behavior is maintained and the new tier field can be introduced gradually). - If both `batching.tier` and legacy knobs are set, validation fails with a clear message to avoid ambiguous precedence (the explicit guidance is: pick tier OR legacy knobs, not both). (4) Config introspection: - Extends `configctl validate` output to include a normalized view of effective tier + effective profile (for debugging config rollouts and Dedicated deployments). - Adds structured error codes for common validation failures (to support Console UX and customer-facing errors later). Files/areas touched (high level): - `control-plane/config/schema/route_policy.proto` (adds tier and profile fields) - `control-plane/config/validation/batching.go` (validation + compatibility rules) - `control-plane/config/normalize/route_policy_normalize.go` (legacy -> tiered normalized representation) - `tools/configctl/validate_cmd.go` (debug output improvements) - `docs/internal/config-schema.md` (internal-only note; public docs are separate) Example config (normalized): route_policies: - name: chat-default model: llama-3.1-70b batching: tier: FAST profiles: FAST: max_wait_ms: 1 max_batch_tokens: 4096 STANDARD: max_wait_ms: 4 max_batch_tokens: 8192 COST_EFFICIENT: max_wait_ms: 10 max_batch_tokens: 16384 Notes: Values above are illustrative only; final recommended defaults per tier/model/hardware are owned by perf/benchmarking work and will land separately. Testing: - Unit tests for schema validation (valid tiers, invalid tiers, missing required fields, range checks). - Golden tests for normalization output (legacy knobs -> normalized tiered profile). - Ran `configctl validate` against production-like snapshots from Hosted + Dedicated staging (no changes required; legacy configs continue to validate). Rollout plan: - Safe to merge behind existing behavior since tier is optional and legacy configs are untouched. - Follow-ups will: (a) wire tier selection to runtime config consumption, (b) add reason codes/telemetry, (c) add feature flagging and rollout controls. Checklist: - [x] Backwards compatibility confirmed with staging config snapshots - [x] Validation errors are actionable (include field path + suggestion) - [x] Added unit/golden tests - [x] No runtime behavior change in this PR Related: - Linear: ENG-18422 - Project: Workload-aware batching defaults (tiered SLO profiles) Review notes / conversation (abridged): Priya Natarajan: Please ensure we don’t end up with three different places to set batching (legacy knobs, tier, per-tier profiles) without clear mutual exclusivity. Ethan Park: Agreed. Added explicit validation to fail if `tier` is set alongside legacy knobs; also updated normalize logic to only synthesize a `STANDARD` profile when tier is unset. Jordan Lee: Can we avoid `COST_EFFICIENT` vs `COST_EFFICIENT` naming drift across components? Also prefer stable casing in JSON. Ethan Park: Implemented strict enum mapping with JSON strings `fast|standard|cost_efficient` and canonicalized output in `configctl`. Added tests to ensure round-trip stability. Sean Gallagher: Please add guardrails for negative/zero limits; also want error codes for alerting/triage. Ethan Park: Added range checks + `CFG_BATCHING_*` error codes surfaced by `configctl validate` and control plane logs. Approvals: - Priya Natarajan (approved) - Jordan Lee (approved) - Sean Gallagher (approved) CI: build-and-test (pass), configctl-golden (pass), lint (pass). Merge: Squash merged into `main`.
commits: config: add batching tier + per-tier profile fields to route policy schema
validation: enforce mutual exclusivity between legacy batching knobs and tier config
normalize: synthesize STANDARD tier override from legacy knobs when tier unset
tools: configctl validate prints normalized effective batching config
tests: golden + unit tests for tier parsing and normalization
